artifacts.notes:
1,210 leaves at 600.9 x 925.57 points, PDF 1.7, read with pdfinfo. The item's
`_page_numbers.json` assigns a printed page number to 849 of them, the highest
being 827; the gap between 1,210 leaves and 827 printed pages is the book's
several pagination sequences -- the front matter, the main arabic run, and the
bracketed appendix run [176]-[188] -- plus the unnumbered inserted leaves, and is
not evidence of a second book.

WHY IT IS REGISTERED AT ALL, HOLDING NO BYTES. It fixes the page count that the
acquisition brief asked for, it authenticates the images independently of the
derived text, and it is the artifact a leaf-level carve-out would have to be
built over if a later lane attempts one. 176 MB is also, on its own, a reason not
to track a file this repository has no affirmative basis to distribute.
artifacts.rights_basis:
The page images this text layer was made from, and the same finding governs
them. Unresolved for the reason set out in full on the sibling text artifact
artifact.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense.vatican-typica-1924.missale-bracarense-1924-text-88d4a147:
the 1924 typical edition clears the pre-1931 United States line as derived for
calendar year 2026, and the scanned volume also carries at least fifteen
supplement leaves and gatherings printed between 1925 and 21 November 1961, which
that line does not reach. A PAGE IMAGE IS THE WORSE OF THE TWO CASES, not the
better one: the Bridgeman argument that a faithful reproduction of a public-domain
page adds no new authorship leaves the reproduction of a 1955 page exactly as
protected as the page. No image of this book is published anywhere in this
repository and none may be. See src/sources/inventories/missale-bracarense-rights-v1.toml.

artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of a whole Missal of the
Braga use, 132,548 LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes and no form
feeds. It is registered as a source artifact and nothing more, and it is
deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records. THERE ARE NO PAGE BOUNDARIES
IN THIS FILE, which matters twice over: a line range over it is not a printed-page
range, and the Lasance-style single replayable deletion on printed-page
boundaries therefore cannot be stated from this file alone.

OCR QUALITY, AND IT IS GOOD. Measured here by scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a Latin
function-word share of 0.191 over 449,452 tokens, English 0.0298, classified
`prose-latin` -- the same class as the 1862 Pustet and far above the 0.0788 of the
1570 blackletter. The item's own metadata records `ocr_detected_lang = la` at
confidence 1.0000, `ocr_detected_script = Latin` at 0.9364, 300 ppi, and
`page_number_confidence = 81`. The damage that remains is ordinary and
two-columned: this book sets two columns to the page and the scan interleaves
them, so consecutive lines frequently belong to different columns and a sentence
read straight down the file is often two sentences shuffled. Read a locus, do not
read a run.

THE DROPPED INITIALS ARE A SEARCH HAZARD AND ONE OF THEM MATTERS TO THE DATING.
Every large ornamental initial is emitted as line noise or not at all. The bull's
`Inter multiplices` opens at line 43 as `nter multiplices gravesque curas`; the
Assumption Introit of 1950 is stored at line 96689 as `"ignum magnum` and a
literal search for `Signum magnum` finds it only through the running repetitions
a few lines later. Do not rest a negative search on this text layer: absence of a
string is evidence about the layer, not about the book.

BOTH ASSUMPTION MASSES ARE PRESENT, WHICH IS THE ONE PLACE THIS BOOK IS BETTER
OFF THAN THE 1920. The 1924 formulary `IN ASSUMPTIONE B. MARI[AE] V.` with the
Introit `[G]audeamus omnes in Domino` stands at lines 96594-96600, and the 1950
formulary `Die 15 Augusti / IN ASSUMPTIONE B. MARIA V.` with `Signum magnum`
stands at lines 96685-96689. So the later leaf sits BESIDE the text it displaced
in use rather than in place of it, and deleting it would not leave 15 August
without a Mass -- the defect that killed the carve-out route on the 1920. That
does not rescue the route here; see the rights record. It is recorded because the
difference between the two books is real and a later lane should not inherit the
1920's reasoning wholesale.

WHAT THE TEXT LAYER CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Title page at
lines 1-36, ending `ROME` / `TYPIS POLYGLOTTIS VATICANIS` / `MDCCCCXXIV`; the
bull Inter multiplices gravesque curas from line 43, subscribed at its close by
Cardinal Vico and Maurus Rigal; the decree of the Sacred Congregation of Rites
headed `DECRETUM` at line 297 and dated `Die 9 Decembris 1924.` at line 341; the
computistical matter and tables of movable feasts from about line 450, the
kalendar from about line 1400; the temporal from about line 4500; the sanctoral
running from `Die 1 Januarii` at line 65167 to `Die 26 Novembris` at line 110006,
with the inserted leaves out of date order inside it; the Masses of the dead from
about line 125990; the appendices in bracketed pagination [176]-[188] -- the
blessings and the `TONI COMMUNES MISSAE` -- from about line 130900; and the two
latest supplement leaves, the Queenship and St Pius X, standing after the tones
at lines 131332 and 131563 where the volume ends. The file ends in the index of
blessings and tones, which is where the book ends and not where the scan was cut
short.

IDENTITY. Internet Archive item `missale-bracarense-1924`, uploaded 2026-02-01 by
a private uploader, credited `Igreja Catolica, Pio XI, Arquidiocese de Braga,
D. Manuel Vieira de Matos, 'Alma Bracarense' website`, in collection `opensource`,
with no rights or licence field. The PDF was assembled with PDF24 and iLovePDF on
31 January 2026 from the sectional scans published by the Alma Bracarense blog;
that blog's own missal page describes the sections and says nothing about
supplements or added Masses, so NOBODY UPSTREAM FLAGGED THE ACCRETION and it is
visible only in the bytes. The companion page-image artifact of the same scan is
artifact.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense.vatican-typica-1924.missale-bracarense-1924-scan-2be6474d,
1,210 leaves.

WHAT A READER OF THIS BOOK MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF IT. Nothing
in this repository has read a unit of the Braga use, and this artifact does not
make it readable: `read_from = "not-read"` on the witness row in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record. The next lane needs, in order: a leaf
map that separates 1924 pages from supplement pages, which the item's per-leaf
OCR (`_djvu.xml`, `_hocr.html`, `_page_numbers.json`) can support and this file
cannot; a rights disposition for whichever stratum it means to quote; and then
passage records with real loci over exact bytes, not line ranges standing in for
liturgical identity.
artifacts.rights_basis:
UNRESOLVED, AND THE REASON IS THAT THESE BYTES ARE NOT A 1924 PRINTING
THROUGHOUT. The commissioning brief expected `tracked` and `public-domain` on
the pre-1931 United States line. The line clears the 1924 edition and does not
clear this file, and the difference was found by reading the file rather than by
trusting the year in its identifier. This is the second time in two days that a
missal folded in on a publication date turned out to carry later matter: the
first was artifact.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1920, withdrawn
on 2026-08-02 when its appendix proved to print a Mass granted to a society
erected in 1970. The check that caught this one was run because that one
happened.

WHAT THE LINE IS, AND THE YEAR IT WAS DERIVED FOR. Any work first published
outside the United States before 1931 is out of United States copyright; that is
the line guidance/missals.md records from Cornell's public-domain chart as
current on 1 January 2026. THE LINE MOVES EVERY JANUARY -- guidance/missals.md:249
states it in terms -- so it is written here as derived for calendar year 2026 and
not as a standing rule: on 1 January 2027 it becomes before 1932, and a later
reader must re-derive it rather than quote this sentence. Publication of the
typical edition in 1924 clears the 2026 line by seven years and the 2027 line by
eight. Nothing in this record disturbs that; see `[the_1924_edition]` in
src/sources/inventories/missale-bracarense-rights-v1.toml.

WHAT IS IN THE FILE THAT 1924 DOES NOT COVER. Every locus below is a physical
line of the file named by `sha256`, one-based as `grep -n` counts, read here on
2026-08-02. Fifteen or more supplement leaves and gatherings are bound into the
scanned volume, each with its own approbation and imprimatur, the latest dated
21 NOVEMBER 1961 (line 84293, `*carae. die 21 Nov., f961`, subscribed
`$ ANTONIUS, Archiepiscopus Bracarensis`). The feasts they print did not exist
when this Missal was promulgated:

  D. N. Jesu Christi Regis, `DOMINICA ULTIMA OCTOBRIS / IN FESTO / D. NOSTRI
  JESU CHRISTI REGIS` at line 106042 -- instituted by Quas primas of 11 December
  1925, a year and three days after the decree that made this edition typical;

  S. Pii Papae X, `DIE 3 SEPTEMBRIS` at line 131563 with the collect
  `Deus, qui ad tuendam catholicam fidem, et universa in Christo instauranda
  sanctum Pium, Summum Pontificem` following -- canonized 29 May 1954. THE SAME
  SAINT, IN THE SAME PLACE IN THE BOOK, AS THE 1920's DECISIVE FINDING;

  Beatae Mariae Virginis Reginae, `DIE 31 MAJI` at line 131332 -- the Queenship,
  instituted by Ad caeli Reginam of 11 October 1954;

  S. Joseph Opificis, `DIE I MAJI / IN SOLEMNITATE / S. JOSEPH OPIFICIS, SPONSI
  B. MARIAE V., CONF., OPIFICUM PATRONI` at lines 77511-77517 -- instituted 1955;

  S. Gregorii Barbadici at line 84178 and S. Antonii Mariae Claret at line 84234,
  both headed `3. classis` (lines 84181, 84240) -- Barbarigo was canonized 26 May
  1960, Claret 7 May 1950, and the class ranks are the vocabulary of the 1960
  Code of Rubrics, which the rest of this book does not use anywhere;

  S. Joannis Leonardi at line 102965, canonized 1938; S. Joannis de Brito at
  lines 69703 and 69880, canonized 22 June 1947; S. Joannis Mariae Vianney at
  line 95438, canonized 1925 and given 9 August in 1928; S. Joannis Eudes at
  line 97219 and S. Petri Canisii at line 76592, both canonized 1925;

  and the Assumption in the Mass Signum magnum of 1950, whose Introit stands at
  line 96689 as `"ignum magnum appáruit in caelo` -- the dropped ornamental S
  again, exactly the loss that made the 1920 look seven years earlier than it was.

The subscriptions that date the leaves, read in the bytes: Sacred Congregation of
Rites approbations at lines 102248 (17 May 1925, subscribed Alexander Verde),
106395 (7 April 1927), 97346 (31 May 1928), 82136 (2 April 1929), 104265
(14 October 1929), 79629 (2 February 1932), 119334 and 121826 (24 December 1935),
110294 (9 January 1942, with `Acta Apostolice Sedis, 13 Aprilis 1942` at line
110298); Braga imprimaturs at lines 76671 (24 November 1926), 97361 (19 August
1928), 102257 (3 October 1928), 79634 and 109091 (2 October 1932), 71812
(5 September 1933), 119346 and 121841 (3 April 1936), 68602 (Turin 6 May 1936,
Braga 5 August 1936), 103203 (9 October 1940), 110366 (24 May 1947), 69954
(5 November 1953), 131516 (15 March 1955), 131724 (5 July 1955), 91332
(November 1958), 84293 (21 November 1961); a Braga printer's imprint
`BRACARJE — Sumpibus ex Typis Universalis` at line 119353, which is not the
Vatican Polyglot Press of the title page; and a Portuguese-language note at line
125962 citing `A S. C. dos Ritos (Decreto de 27 de Novembro de 1957)`.

WHY THE BOOK UNDER THE SUPPLEMENT IS STILL A 1924 IMPRESSION, STATED SO THE
FINDING IS NOT OVERREAD. The title page reads MDCCCCXXIV at line 36; the kalendar
at lines 1400-2400 lists none of the feasts above; the table of movable feasts
opens at 1923; the ranks in the body are duplex, semiduplex and simplex
throughout and `3. classis` occurs exactly twice, both on inserted leaves. So
this is not a late reprint wearing an old date. It is a 1924 book that stayed in
use, with the additions of thirty-seven years bound into it -- which is what
happens to the altar book of a living rite, and is precisely why a living rite's
twentieth-century missal is a harder acquisition than a dead rite's sixteenth-
century one.

WHY BRIDGEMAN DOES NOT REACH IT, WHICH IS THE CONFLATION THIS RECORD REFUSES. A
faithful mechanical reproduction of a public-domain work is not original
authorship (Bridgeman Art Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y.
1999)), and machine optical character recognition adds no human authorship on top
of it: this text layer was produced autonomously by tesseract 5.3.0-6-g76ae run
with `-l lat`, per the item's own `ocr` and `ocr_parameters` fields, and there is
no author to hold a right in it. THAT ARGUMENT IS ABOUT THE LAYER AND NOT ABOUT
WHAT WAS PHOTOGRAPHED. Bridgeman frees a scan of public-domain matter; it says
nothing whatever about a scan of matter first published in 1955, which is
protected in its own right and whose scan is a copy of it. `tracked` in this
repository means the exact artifact is lawful to distribute (guidance/sources.md:
375-400), and the exact artifact is 3,210,801 bytes of which an unmeasured but
plainly nonzero part is a photograph of pages composed between 1925 and 1961. So
the file may not sit in Git, and who holds what in the supplement is open. See
`[the_supplement]` in the rights record for the URAA analysis that would have to
be run before any of it could be cleared, and `[routes_examined_and_refused]` for
why a carve-out was not attempted.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the item carries no rights or licence field.
guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds the first two insufficient for `tracked`, and
the third was never a basis in either direction -- this item's `licenseurl` is
absent, and had it carried a Public Domain Mark that would have changed nothing,
for the reason src/sources/inventories/lt-hist-rights-audit-v1.toml gives.

edition.authority: Pius XI, bull Inter multiplices gravesque curas of 8 December 1924, printed at the head of the book and subscribed A. Card. VICO, Ep. Portuen. et S. Rufinae and Maurus Rigal, Canc. Ap. Tabularii Praefectus; executed the next day by the Sacred Congregation of Rites, decree of 9 December 1924, operative clause Vaticana hujus Missalis editio pro typica habenda est, with later printings omnino conformandae erunt, ita ut in iis nihil immutare fas sit, subscribed A. Card. VICO, S. R. C. Praefectus and Alexander Verde, S. R. C. Secretarius
edition.jurisdiction: Rite of Braga, archdiocese of Braga
edition.notes:
THE ONLY TWENTIETH-CENTURY TYPICAL EDITION OF A LATIN USE THIS PROJECT CAN
REACH WHOLE, and the reason the Braga line is where the all-Latin-rites scope
starts: the book and both its promulgating instruments are in hand, and the
instruments are printed in the book's own front matter rather than reconstructed
from a gazette. Both were read in the bytes -- the bull opening at line 43 of the
text layer named on the artifact record, with its ornamental I dropped, as
`nter multiplices gravesque curas`, and the decree headed `DECRETUM` at line 297
and dated `Die 9 Decembris 1924.` at line 341.

THE IMPRINT IS THE VATICAN POLYGLOT PRESS AT ROME, WHICH CORRECTS A RECORDED
REASON. src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml and
src/sources/inventories/missal-acquisition-audit-v1.toml both describe this book
as `an ARCHDIOCESAN book rather than a Holy See imprint`, and give that as the
second limb of its rights basis. The book's own title page says otherwise: lines
33 to 36 read `ROME` (for ROMAE), `TYPIS POLYGLOTTIS VATICANIS`, `MDCCCCXXIV`,
and the Congregation's decree calls the edition Vaticana in terms. What is
archdiocesan is the SOLLICITUDO -- the Archbishop of Braga procured the printing
and the rite is his church's -- and what is Vatican is the press. The correction
costs the rights position nothing, because the operative limb was never the
imprint but the year, and 1924 is before the pre-1931 United States line
whoever set the type. It is recorded because a rights basis with a false limb in
it is a basis nobody can check. The edition slug follows the imprint and the
decree, on the pattern of missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1920.

THIS RECORD NAMES THE TYPICAL EDITION. THE ONE COPY SCANNED IS THAT EDITION PLUS
THIRTY-SEVEN YEARS OF BOUND-IN SUPPLEMENT, and the artifact record is where that
is measured. The body of the scanned volume is consistent throughout with a 1924
impression: the kalendar at lines 1400-2400 carries no feast instituted after
1924, the ranks are the pre-1960 duplex, semiduplex and simplex, and the table of
movable feasts opens at 1923. Bound into it are at least fifteen later leaves and
gatherings, each carrying its own approbation of the Sacred Congregation of Rites
and its own Braga imprimatur, dated from 1925 to 21 November 1961, and printing
feasts that did not exist in 1924 -- Christ the King of 1925, St John de Brito of
1947, St Joseph the Worker of 1955, the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary of
1954, St Pius X of 1954, and more. They are additions to a Missal of a living use
made in the ordinary way, by the archdiocese, over the working life of the book;
they are also matter first published well after the line this edition clears, so
the artifacts stand `remote` and `unresolved` and no byte of them is in Git. The
1924 edition ITSELF is untouched by that: published in 1924, out of United States
copyright, and under 17 U.S.C. 103(b) no later supplement's copyright enlarges
anything in it. See src/sources/inventories/missale-bracarense-rights-v1.toml.

WHAT NO EDGE IS DRAWN FROM. The Braga use is far older than this edition -- a
1558 printing is at the Bibliotheque nationale de France, a 1538 at the
Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal, and the 1498 editio princeps has four recorded
copies and no located facsimile -- and none of them is held here, so this record
claims no descent from them. The act history carries the same silence as a root
station with reasons: src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml, act
inter-multiplices-gravesque-curas-1924.

work.author: Archdiocese of Braga
work.description: The altar book of the Rite of Braga -- the Latin use of the archdiocese of Braga, primatial see of the Spains, one of the diocesan uses left standing by the exempting clause of Quo primum. It is a Missal in the ordinary sense, carrying its own kalendar, general rubrics, Ordo Missae and Canon, temporal and sanctoral cycles, Commons, votive and Requiem Masses, blessings and Mass tones. IT IS NOT THE MISSALE ROMANUM AND MUST NOT BE FILED WITH IT. work.catholic-church.missale-romanum is the Roman Rite's book; this is a different rite's, and the only edge this repository draws between them is that the same Congregation of Rites signed both promulgations -- an authority in common, not a descent. The distinction is the reason src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml draws no edge from the Roman line into the Braga line, and it is why this work is registered under the archdiocese rather than under the Catholic Church at large.
